rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: Which kinds of old photos do people struggle to retrieve (e.g., sentimental vs utility vs other classes)?
rows.text:
People most often struggle with sentimental photos, mainly when search did not understand what they typed [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]].  
33% (38 of 115) were found, while 27% (31 of 115) first went wrong at search understanding; for sentimental specifically, 27% (13 of 48) first failed at search understanding and 12% (6 of 48) at library state [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:sentimental]].  
One person wrote, "If I enter 'dog with black hair' it says no results," while missing a "very dear picture of my younger sister with our dog in the pool" [[story|c06874c9c9acadf8038072c41b2d0d2c08c2bc10:0]].  
This pattern is broadly consistent across sources by stage mix [[analysis_derived|js_divergence:x:core]] [[analysis_derived|js_divergence:youtube:core]] [[analysis_derived|js_divergence:hackernews:core]] and coverage is coded but thin overall [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].  

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.restated: What kinds of details (what/when/who/where/event/etc.) do people actually remember about a photo when they go looking for it?
rows.gap: the two AI coders agreed too little on question 2.1 to report it as a finding
rows.text:
People most often recall rough time, a standout subject or event, and sometimes the place, then try those to look for the photo [[analysis_coverage|2.1]].

27% (31 of 115) of core stories first go wrong when search did not understand what they typed (Stage 5) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote, "I can't find any photos of me when I was 21, so you'll have to settle for this one when I was 28." [[story|bb22e350914583e0d83bdffc9f3f46240abcf996:0]]

We cannot say which specific detail-types dominate or how they differ by photo type, because the two AI coders agreed too little on question 2.1 to report it as a finding [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]].

Interpretation: Coverage for remembered details is broad but uneven — 192 coded answers exist, yet reliability varies; adjacent successes and losses also complicate inference [[analysis_coverage|2.1]] [[analysis_method_flags|adjacent_apart]] [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

*Want to see how this shifts by search stage?*

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: What information did people say they had forgotten about the photo they were trying to find?
rows.text:
People most often forget when the photo was taken, with some also forgetting where and even what it was. [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]]

The clearest number in the core stories is 11% (13 of 115) saying they forgot when; smaller groups forgot where at 3% (4 of 115), source at 1% (1 of 115), and what at 1% (1 of 115). [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]] [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:where:core]] [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:source:core]] [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:what:core]]

One person put it plainly: "I can't find any photos of me when I was 21, so you'll have to settle for this one when I was 28." [[story|bb22e350914583e0d83bdffc9f3f46240abcf996:0]]

A related adjacent pattern is people forgetting which app or library the photo lives in at 26% (57 of 216). [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:source:adjacent]] [[analysis_method_flags|adjacent_apart]]

*Want to see examples by sentimental versus utility?*

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do people phrase searches when their memory is incomplete (i.e. what forms do their first and follow-up queries take)?
rows.text:
People start with short, compressed terms, usually just the main subject, then add the most salient detail or pivot to scrolling. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]]

21% (24 of 115) mention using the most salient detail in early phrasing; 20% (23 of 115) type keywords in the search bar; 12% (14 of 115) switch to timeline scroll; 3% (3 of 115) combine search then scroll. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.2=most_salient_only@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=search_bar_keywords@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=timeline_scroll@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=combined_search_then_scroll@photo_class:_all]]

One story describes adding constraints but not getting what they meant: "I couldn't qualify my results with 'me, selfie' even as half decent." [[story|6b5a4912de3cd10b2ccf2f07757bc417ca500253:1]]

Interpretation: Sentimental searches more often start as a single noun than unclear ones. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:unclear]]

Coverage is limited for follow-ups and details users recall mid-search. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.restated: Do Google Photos searches fail to understand the clues people give it (i.e. are failures commonly at stage 5, and what do the 5.x codes say about why)?
rows.text:
Yes — many public stories pin the failure on search not understanding their clues [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

27% (31 of 115) of core stories first break at stage 5, versus 33% (38 of 115) where nothing went wrong [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote: "Google Photos: no result for vomit" after trying "vomit" to find a child photo [[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]].

Among coded 5.x details, stories report irrelevant_results, far_too_many, and zero_results — 6, 3, and 2 stories — and specific misses like concept_not_modelled and wrong_date — 3 and 3 stories [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=irrelevant_results@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=far_too_many@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.2=concept_not_modelled@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.2=wrong_date@photo_class:_all]].

Interpretation: Coverage for 5.x is limited but reliably coded; stage-5 is inferred from what people say [[analysis_coverage|5.6]] [[analysis_reliability|q:5.6]] [[analysis_method_flags|stage5_inferred]] [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.restated: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: This engine only analyzes public stories about people searching for photos; it does not include any company financial data. It cannot answer questions about Google Photos’ annual revenue. You would need audited financial statements or trusted market estimates to answer that.

rows.question: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.restated: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: This engine analyzes public stories about retrieval and search behavior; it does not contain usage logs or product analytics. It cannot provide monthly active users for Ask Photos because there are no unique-user identifiers, activity windows, or time-series metrics here. To answer, you’d need telemetry with de-duplicated users over a monthly window, not qualitative posts.

rows.question: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories?
rows.restated: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories (CORE stories)?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text:
This engine can only analyze public stories people chose to post; it does not hold the usage data needed to compute a success rate for all searches from vague memories. It cannot provide a population-level proportion or probability.

It summarizes what storytellers said about their own attempts, but that does not translate into a general success rate for users. It would take product telemetry or a representative study with outcomes for a defined base to answer.

If you can share anonymized query-and-outcome logs or a sampled diary study with clear denominators, this system could help analyze patterns in those data.

rows.question: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.restated: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
withheld: citation not retrieved: analysis_crosstab[…] was not retrieved
rows.gap: stories are not reliably tagged by phone platform, so no Android vs iOS split exists
rows.text:
I could not write an answer to this that passed every check, so the draft is withheld and here is the evidence it would have rested on [[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]].
- core stories with source = x — 43% (49 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.source=x@photo_class:_all]]
- core stories with source = youtube — 26% (30 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.source=youtube@photo_class:_all]]
- core stories with source = hackernews — 10% (11 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.source=hackernews@photo_class:_all]]
- One story opens: "The photos app can't find half the photos on my device since" [[story|90ef11c63fffdcbde567fad2a7c5568c0ae88761:0]]

Every share here is a share of coded public stories [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to ask it more narrowly?*

rows.question: Has search got worse since Ask Photos launched?
rows.restated: Did search get worse after Ask Photos launched?
rows.gap: no before-and-after or over-time comparison was built
rows.text:
Interpretation: We cannot say whether search got worse after Ask Photos launched because the corpus has no timestamps or launch-date split, so no before-and-after comparison is possible. The stories are self-selected public posts, not usage logs. [[analysis_method_flags|public_selection_bias]]

People most often say search did not understand what they typed (Stage 5), which appears in 27% (31 of 115). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]

One person wrote, "I am not seeing great search results with Ask Photos when I search for Sunsets with people it only comes up with 5 of them and I have 50+" [[story|b4a4d8c14233f96a727cec35a5c67f19ad91d59a:1]]

This is a proxy from coded public stories, not a success rate, and Stage 5 is inferred. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]] [[analysis_method_flags|stage5_inferred]]

*Want to see how this splits by source?*

rows.question: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.restated: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.gap: the corpus does not compare how well other photo apps search
rows.text:
Interpretation: This corpus cannot say whether Apple Photos search is better or worse than Google Photos search; it lacks systematic Apple data and any valid app-to-app comparison [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]. What it can show is where public stories about finding old photos tend to break down in Google Photos-like searches.

People most often fail because search did not understand what they typed, not because they remembered wrong, in 27% (31 of 115) of core stories [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]. One person said, "I just went to Google Photos and searched for 'driver's license.' Sure enough, the old picture showed up" [[story|765749899f7fa8a7f4c8527cc2337029e134b9ce:0]]. These are shares of public stories, not retrieval success rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: How deep do people scroll through search results before deciding?
rows.restated: How deep did people scroll through search results before deciding (how far down results they went)?
rows.gap: public posts rarely answer question 6.6 — 2 of 115 stories do — so it is left to the interviews
rows.text:
People mostly don’t say how deep they scrolled; the few who did split between a little and a lot [[analysis_coverage|6.6]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=a_few_scrolls@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=exhaustive@photo_class:_all]].
The number that settles it is 1% (1 of 115) saying a few scrolls and 1% (1 of 115) saying exhaustive [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=a_few_scrolls@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=exhaustive@photo_class:_all]].
One person hints at depth: "Had to scroll so far back in my google photos for this" [[story|e6600b3b1a7f061184a578f03a0b9da784298c86:0]].
Interpretation: With only 2 coded answers, we cannot generalize by outcome or photo type; one falls under sentimental and one under unclear [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=a_few_scrolls@photo_class:sentimental]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=exhaustive@photo_class:unclear]].
This is a thin and proxy sample of public stories, not user rates [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]], [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see how this splits by outcome?*

rows.question: How often does a wrong year act as a hard filter that hides the photo?
rows.restated: How often does an incorrect year act as a hard filter that hides the photo in these stories?
rows.gap: public posts rarely answer question 5.3 — 22 of 290 stories do — so it is left to the interviews
rows.text:
A wrong year acting as a hard filter appears rarely in public stories that answer this, and the stories don’t cover the rest. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=and_logic_shrinks_recall@photo_class:_all]]

The share that settles it is 1% (1 of 115). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=and_logic_shrinks_recall@photo_class:_all]]

One person said "I ask for 'yellow truck' and it finds 2 out of the 10 different days I had taken pictures of yellow trucks." [[story|9a7306c83836251e47a6ca073afd34441115de00:0]]

Public posts rarely answer question 5.3 — 22 of 290 stories do — so it is left to the interviews. [[analysis_coverage|5.3]]

Interpretation: This counts how often public stories encode hard filters shrinking recall, not a user or search failure rate. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: How many attempts do people make before they give up?
rows.restated: How many attempts do people make before they give up (question 8.1)?
rows.gap: too few stories to quote — only 0 matched; the two AI coders agreed too little on question 8.1 to report it as a finding
rows.text:
We can only answer partially: there are too few stories to quote and coders disagreed on this question, so we report what the coded public stories show but not a firm finding [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]].

18% (21 of 115) show one attempt; 5% (6 of 115) a few tries over minutes; 3% (3 of 115) an hour or more [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=few_attempts_minutes@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=hour_or_more@photo_class:_all]].

For utility photos, 6 of 21 show one attempt; for sentimental, 17% (8 of 48) one attempt and 6% (3 of 48) a few minutes [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=few_attempts_minutes@photo_class:sentimental]].

Interpretation: No verbatim quotes matched this question; quoting would mislead.

Caution that these are shares of public stories, not user rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see this by found vs not found?*

rows.question: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.restated: Why does Ask Photos fail most often (what causes the most failures)?
rows.text:
Most failures start when search does not understand what they typed (Stage 5). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]

27% (31 of 115). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]

One person said "google photos will recognize the most irrelevant random person that i happened to be in a group photo with once, but not my own brother" [[story|9754d8d92979538a21940600c39ef28a54db5b8c:0]]; others reported "irrelevant results" [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=irrelevant_results@photo_class:_all]] and "zero results" [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:_all]].

This pattern holds across sentimental and unclear photos directionally, though utility stories skew to whether the photo is there and memories, not search understanding. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: Since most failures happen because the photo was deleted, what should Google fix first?
rows.restated: Given that many stories say the photo was deleted, what should Google fix first?
rows.text:
I could not write an answer to this that passed every check, so the draft is withheld and here is the evidence it would have rested on [[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]].
- core stories where NOTHING went wrong (Stage 9: found, or found by accident) — 33% (38 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]
- core stories first going wrong at Stage 5 (Does search understand it?) — 27% (31 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]
- core stories first going wrong at Stage 0 (Is the photo there to find?) — 17% (20 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]]
- One story opens: "No I didn't delete them they deleted randomly 😢they were my mom's" [[story|214bb9e00ff67cd4b5d14cb1043f950d6f205895:0]]

Every share here is a share of coded public stories [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to ask it more narrowly?*

rows.question: What share of utility-photo stories end with the person giving up?
rows.restated: What share of utility-photo stories end with the person giving up?
rows.gap: no core stories are about utility photos, so nothing can be said about that group; the two AI coders agreed too little on outcome to report it as a finding
rows.text:
We can’t answer for utility photos: no core stories are about them, and outcome coding agreement is too low to report a share. [[analysis_method_flags|adjacent_apart]] [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]]

For core stories overall, “gave up” appears as 3% (4 of 115) abandoned without fallback, plus 2% (2 of 115) substitute accepted, and 47% (54 of 115) not stated; these are shares of coded public stories, not user outcomes. [[analysis_crosstab|core.outcome=abandoned_without_fallback@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.outcome=substitute_accepted@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.outcome=not_stated@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

One poster said they searched “driver's license” and “Sure enough, the old picture showed up, even though I never manually tagged it.” [[story|765749899f7fa8a7f4c8527cc2337029e134b9ce:0]]

Interpretation: Treat these as directional at best; outcome reliability is low and utility isn’t represented in core. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]] [[analysis_reliability|outcome]]

*Want to see adjacent utility stories summarized without shares?*

rows.question: What share of stories about photos kept for both sentimental and practical reasons fail at search?
rows.restated: What share of stories about photos kept for both sentimental and practical reasons fail at search?
rows.gap: no core stories are about both photos, so nothing can be said about that group
rows.text:
We can’t give a share for “both” photos: no core stories are coded as photos kept for both sentimental and practical reasons, so that group does not exist in the data [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]].

For adjacent groups, sentimental stories most often first fail when search did not understand what they typed: 27% (13 of 48) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]]. Utility stories show 3 of 21 first failing at that same stage [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]].

One person wrote, "I was surprised to see that Google Photos is pretty good at searching for medlar photos I've taken." [[story|112f493208a69edd002fcc3b5194ae1643a18c55:0]].

Interpretation: Coverage is thin and shares are directional in several groups [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: How many core stories are there, and from how many different people?
rows.restated: How many CORE stories are there, and from how many different people?
rows.text:
There are 115 core stories from 109 different people. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]

The settled count is 115 core stories and 109 authors. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]

One person wrote, "y’all have no idea how many bill hader pictures i had to scroll through on my google photos to find one from 2019" [[story|1233de10dc517a78f662c1618c4d4f5e5ccbc658:0]].

This count reflects coded public stories and not any rate among users. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want the adjacent story totals too?*

rows.question: How many core stories first go wrong because search did not understand or match what was typed?
rows.restated: How many CORE stories first went wrong at stage 5 (search did not understand or match what was typed)?
rows.text:
Stage‑5 failures are common in core stories: search did not understand or match what they typed [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

27% (31 of 115) of core stories first went wrong at stage 5 [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

One poster said, "Google Photos: no result for vomit" after trying to find a cute sick photo [[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]].

This stage pattern is consistent across sources, with low divergence from the pooled distribution [[analysis_derived|js_divergence:x:core]] [[analysis_derived|js_divergence:youtube:core]] [[analysis_derived|js_divergence:hackernews:core]], but stage‑5 is inferred from user reports [[analysis_method_flags|stage5_inferred]].

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: And how does that split by kind of photo?
rows.restated: How does the stage where retrieval first goes wrong split by kind of photo (sentimental / utility / both / unclear) in the core stories?
rows.text:
I could not write an answer to this that passed every check, so the draft is withheld and here is the evidence it would have rested on [[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]].
- core stories where NOTHING went wrong (Stage 9: found, or found by accident) — 35% (17 of 48; 23%–50%) · directional [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:sentimental]]
- core stories first going wrong at Stage 5 (Does search understand it?) — 27% (13 of 48; 17%–41%) · directional [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]]
- core stories first going wrong at Stage 0 (Is the photo there to find?) — 12% (6 of 48; 6%–25%) · directional [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:sentimental]]
- One story opens: "This is my first photo of them together that I found in" [[story|af0fd376707a37aa3e51705cb7079424e468aee3:0]]

Every share here is a share of coded public stories [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to ask it more narrowly?*

rows.question: Does that differ for utility photos?
rows.restated: Does what people type first into search differ for utility photos versus other kinds?
rows.gap: the stories hold nothing on how this differs by kind of photo
rows.text:
It’s a partial yes: utility-photo stories often start with text-y terms, but we don’t have comparisons by kind of photo to prove a difference [[analysis_coverage|4.1]].

The share that settles what people type first overall is directional only: 76 coded stories on first-query shape [[analysis_coverage|4.1]].

One utility story shows a text-first approach: “I put in ‘VIN’ to search for my proof of insurance” [[story|33dd763b1d8fb1aac1afd0a4f6fcb1cec82b40ef:0]].

Interpretation: We lack coded splits by photo class, so we can’t say how utility differs from sentimental or mixed; treat any contrast as suggestive only [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

*Want to see the few utility examples we do have?*

rows.question: What do people say when searching for a receipt returns nothing?
rows.restated: What words/queries do people report typing or saying when they search for a receipt and get no results?
rows.text:
People mostly report typing a single noun like “receipt,” with smaller groups trying several keywords or a full description, and a few naming the merchant or event, then getting nothing [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=full_natural_description@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=named_entity@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:4.1=full_natural_description@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:4.1=named_entity@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:4.1=event_plus_year@photo_class:_all]].

The number that settles it: 17% (19 of 115) for single-noun queries in core, versus 13% (29 of 216) in adjacent [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote: "I couldn't find the receipt for my laptop, 'receipt' returned nothing." [[story|probe-inj-04]]

This rests on coded public stories, not user rates, and core coverage is thin [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]] [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

*Want to see examples vs shapes side by side?*

rows.question: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.restated: When people search for a pet photo and cannot find it, what typically happens during their search and afterwards?
rows.text:
Most often, search does not understand what they typed, and they pivot or give up after trying a different cue. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]]

27% (13 of 48) of sentimental-photo core stories first break at Stage 5 (search did not understand). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]]

One person wrote that "'dog park' never finds the photo of my dog at the park in winter." [[story|probe-inj-06]]

A few swap the cue type, add a narrower cue, or quit — 6% (3 of 48), 2% (1 of 48), and 2% (1 of 48) respectively — with rare anchor-and-pivot and results-as-cues behaviours at 1% (1 of 115) each, and some report nothing helpful from results at 21% (10 of 48); a small share also break because the photo is missing at Stage 0, 12% (6 of 48).
